boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Haw's Shop record (May 28, 1864) in Grant's Overland Campaign [May-June 1864]. It falls inside the Totopotomoy Creek record's interval (VA057); Wilson's June 3 fight at Hawes's Shop belongs to Cold Harbor's interval. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Divisions and the live field zero. NPS names Gregg's division supported by Torbert's against Fitzhugh Lee's and Hampton's divisions, later reinforced by Butler's brigade. Sheridan's report says the force appeared to be the enemy's cavalry corps and a South Carolina brigade; Humphreys relays Sheridan that the brigade was reported 4,000 strong, but cites Fitzhugh Lee for two divisions of two brigades each and Butler's brigade.
claims.rationale: The identifications differ; the 4,000 is a report relayed by Sheridan, not a return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

open_questions: Gregg's, Torbert's, Custer's, Hampton's and Fitzhugh Lee's reports and the returns remain deferred; Sheridan's May 28 dispatches were not located in the selected range.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan, and it shares headquarters papers with Meade's and Sheridan's reports. Meade's, Sheridan's, Hampton's, Butler's and Wild's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Parts 1 and 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
